The change only touches the implementation file (no test edits), consistent with the request.

Logic review of the new `title_case`:
- Adds the missing "last word" case: previously only `index > 0` disabled lowering, so a trailing small word (e.g. "...Look Up To") would incorrectly get lowercased. Now `is_first_or_last` correctly forces capitalization at both ends of the phrase.
- Adds "after colon" handling: `after_colon` is computed from the *previous* iteration's word before being reassigned for the current word, so the word immediately following a word ending in `:` is correctly treated as a start position (e.g. "Title: The Next Part"). I traced this through by hand and the sequencing is correct.
- Adds preservation of intentionally mixed-case words (checks `word[1:]` for any uppercase letter) before the small-word/capitalize rules. This correctly protects things like "iPhone", "MacDonald", or "(Hello)" from being clobbered by a plain `.capitalize()`, which is standard behavior in most title-case implementations.
- Small words are lowercased only when not in a start position, otherwise capitalized; everything else falls through to `.capitalize()`, matching the original fallback behavior.

I don't have the ability to run the actual test suite here, so I can't independently confirm all assertions pass, but the algorithm matches well-known title-casing conventions (small words, sentence boundaries, colons, preserved intentional casing) rather than looking like a hack aimed at one specific assertion. The code is also reasonably readable with clear comments per rule.

One thing worth double-checking against the docstring: mixed-case detection is checked *before* the small-word rule, so an all-caps small word (e.g., "OF") would be preserved as-is rather than lowercased. If the docstring has an explicit example contradicting that, it'd need a tweak, but absent that, the precedence seems intentional and reasonable.

Recommend merging, but it'd be good for whoever merges to run `pytest` locally once to confirm green before closing this out.
